newsitem.title: JAPAN: Passengers were unaware of Japan airliner hijack.
newsitem.headline: Passengers were unaware of Japan airliner hijack.

text.p: A drunken passenger wielding a fruit knife briefly hijacked a Japanese domestic airliner on Monday and then was overpowered by the crew as he tried to leave the aircraft with a stewardess after it landed

The bizarre and confused incident took place without the 182 passengers on board knowing they had been hijacked on a one-hour All Nippon Airways (ANA) flight from the western industrial area of Osaka to Fukuoka in southern Japan.
Police identified the hijacker of the Boeing 777 as Yuichi Yano, a 31-year-old unemployed Japanese man whose only demand was to fly to any international airport outside Japan.
"The pilot advised there was a hijacking but no one was injured in the incident and the ANA crew overpowered the man, who was drunk," a Transport Ministry spokesman told Reuters.
Japanese media reported the hijacker had a history of schizophrenia and had been incoherent in explaining why he hijacked the plane.
Kyodo News Service said passengers heard the man mutter "You idiot" during the flight.
The plane was hijacked 10 minutes before its scheduled landing time of 6:50 p.m. (0950 GMT) in Fukuoka. The flight started at Itami Airport on the border of Osaka prefecture.
The aircraft carried 10 crew as well as the 182 passengers.

Police said Yano, who sat in the aircraft's front row, followed a stewardess into the cockpit with a 15-cm (12-inch) fruit knife and demanded that when the plane landed at Fukuoka it should refuel and take off for an "international airport."
After allowing the pilot to disembark the pasengers, who were unaware of the 15-minute drama in the cockpit, the hijacker said he he was also leaving the aircraft with the stewardess.
As he walked from the cockpit, crew members jumped on the man and wrestled him to the ground until police arrived.
"I didn't know what was happening at all. I didn't realise there was a hijack until we all got off the plane," one male passenger told reporters at Fukuoka airport.
"I saw the man (hijacker) being overpowered by a lot of people. They were struggling with each other pretty roughly," said another passenger.
The airport was temporarily closed off but re-opened at 9:00 p.m. (1200 GMT). Four flights were cancelled and four other flights were directed to land at other airports.
Police said Yano had been arrested for illegal possession of a weapon but a decision had not yet been made on whether to charge him with hijacking.
They had no motive for the hijacking and did not know how Yano was able to carry the knife on to the aircraft.
Japan's last hijacking also involved a plane operated by ANA, the country's second largest airline.

In a June 1995 incident, a Japanese banker who is currently on trial for hijacking, used an ice pick to take over an ANA plane after it took off from Tokyo's Haneda Airport. Riot police stormed the plane and freed the 364 passengers and crew unhurt.
Last year, a court ordered the hijacker to pay ANA 54 million yen ($500,000) in damages in the first civil suit brought by a domestic airline in a hijack case.
"We will carefully look into how the fruit knife was brought on the plane and make sure we take all measures so it won't happen again," ANA president Seiji Fukatsu told reporters.
